summary: Angeles NF's first lookout, on Lookout Mountain above Baldy Village (1915-1927); sources disagree on its end, and only Michelson's concrete piers are described there today.

facts.design: Classic California Region 5 Plan 4A: 20-foot enclosed timber tower with six window panels and a high hip roof
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1927 per the register and a 1927 newspaper; Wikipedia says it burned. The Sunset Peak tower that followed was dismantled around 1974-75. No source describes the site now beyond the Michelson piers
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Angeles National Forest

access.note: No source says whether the summit is open to visitors today

events.note: Register gives 1915; a June 1915 newspaper item reports a lookout station established near Mount San Antonio. Wikipedia says 1914 (see resolved_conflicts)
E.E. Cook to be assigned to the post to locate forest fires (June 1915 item)
E.E. Cook spent eight months of each year at the station (January 1918 item); a windstorm blew in the glass of the tower
Register photo caption: 1926 is the last year in service
Dismantled per the register and the October 1927 Madera Tribune item
Angeles Adventures says the old tower was removed to Sunset Peak; the register and the 1927 item describe a new steel tower replacing it there
Wikipedia only; conflicts with the register, the 1927 newspaper and Angeles Adventures
Albert A. Michelson used the peak for speed-of-light measurements, 1925 to 1929; concrete piers still exist
Registered November 2, 2019 as US 1781, CA 27; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and a June 1915 newspaper item give 1915 (Angeles Adventures says the tower was planned in 1914). Wikipedia gives 1914. The record keeps 1915, and the story gives both.

The register and a 1927 newspaper say the lookout was dismantled. Wikipedia says it burned. Angeles Adventures says the old tower was removed to Sunset Peak, while the register and the 1927 item describe a new steel tower there. The record keeps dismantled in 1927 and flags the rest.

The register and Angeles Adventures identify Old Baldy with Lookout Mountain, and the 1927 item names Baldy Lookout peak. Forest Lookouts files the early station under Mount San Antonio (Old Baldy) and also as Fuego Vista. The register says only that Fuego Vista has been suggested as the same site.

notes_for_editor: Date and fate conflict across sources (see resolved_conflicts). The 1915, 1918 and 1927 newspaper items are reprints quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; I did not see the originals. Staffing comes only from those reprints. The only description of the site today is Wikipedia's note on the Michelson piers. The brief's gone status is supported. Page title on Forest Lookouts is Mount San Antonio (Old Baldy), so the identity question is for the editor.
